first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the observed completion decline and has prior evidence of improving time-to-value and early adoption. Promotional pricing is highly consequential given the competitor threat but requires verification for qualified-revenue durability before displacing an activation-focused experiment. Run a guarded onboarding test with qualified-revenue and retention follow-through measurement.

final.rationale: Run a standard controlled onboarding-simplification experiment. It directly addresses the 4% onboarding-completion decline and is supported by confirmed evidence that shorter onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; prior signup simplification also lifted first-week activation. Do not use promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue short term, the discounted cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive its first renewal cycle, conflicting with the sustainable-revenue objective. Measure activation, qualified conversion, retention, and renewal-proxy outcomes by SMB segment before rollout.
